manifest.prompt: a 5 second looping animation in the style of Figma brand visuals
how_to_read: 1. Read the head first: the first 34 lines hold manifest, essence and routing (Read limit=34, or jq '{manifest, essence, routing}' figma-brand-loop-animation.metadump.json).
2. Pick the route for your job and run its jq: jq '<routing[i].jq>' figma-brand-loop-animation.metadump.json
3. Also pull the anti-keywords and review prompts (checks) for your scope: jq '.anti_keywords, .checks' figma-brand-loop-animation.metadump.json
4. Look up any term (lowercase): jq '.index["<term>"]' figma-brand-loop-animation.metadump.json  -> hits give id + path; not_meant lists senses to avoid.
5. Grep works too: every entry is one line, so grep -n '<word>' figma-brand-loop-animation.metadump.json returns whole entries.

essence.one_sentence: A 5 s loop in Figma's brand look is a seamless repeat of one flat shape system in bright spectrum color, and the seam, not the style, decides whether it works.
essence.summary: Flat primitive shapes, expanded spectrum color on soft gradients, eased motion that settles, and a last frame identical to the first.

formula.full: flat primitive shapes + expanded spectrum color on soft gradient fields + eased motion that animates an action + a seamless 5 s seam
formula.essential: flat shapes, spectrum color, seamless 5 s seam

tensions.text: bold, playful bounce vs precise, calm settle
varied shape language vs one fixed system
poles: one reusable palette and shape vocabulary

generic.positive: A seamless 5-second looping motion piece in the style of Figma brand visuals: a bold, playful, varied arrangement of flat primitive shapes (circles, squares, blobs, starbursts) in an expanded spectrum of bright colors, with a signature purple used for emphasis, sitting on soft gradient fields. Shapes animate an action: a shape moves along one designed path, reorders or activates, eased with an ease-out on the way out and an ease-in-out on the return, and it settles rather than bouncing. Flat vector surfaces with hairline outlines or soft-shadow depth. Dynamic composition: shapes arranged as activities in one shared space with corner handles and selection-style cues. The last frame matches the first exactly in position, color and scale, so the repeat is invisible. A few shapes travel one designed path with clear negative space and crisp edges. One option: a shape exits one edge of the frame and re-enters from the other, with the seam hidden off-screen.
generic.constraints: Exactly 5 s; last frame identical to the first in position, color and scale. At most three flashes in any one-second period. Brand shape language only, no logo or wordmark as a mark. Flat vector shapes, not a 3D render.
generic.negative: 3D render, glossy surface, neon gradient blob, bouncing spinner, confetti burst, rapid flashing, seam jump, Figma logo, wordmark, product UI
generic.notes: Choices a user may vary, phrased as options: loop type (cyclic orbit, ping-pong scale pulse, shape travel wrap, stepped holds) and motion character (playful bounce vs precise settle). See /loop_motion/options and /brand_look/options.

ak-animation-stills.instead: motion on screen, with eased movement between states

ak-neon-gradient-blob.instead: flat multi-color geometric shapes on soft gradients, with hairline or soft-shadow depth

ak-random-confetti-burst.instead: a few geometric shapes travel along one designed path and return on the loop

ak-flash-burst.instead: steady color shifts with at most three flashes in any one-second period

ak-loop-seam-jump.term: visible jump at the loop seam
ak-loop-seam-jump.instead: last frame identical in position and color to the first frame, so the repeat is invisible

k-loop-length.text: The loop runs exactly 5 s before it repeats.

test.spec: timeline duration equals 5 s; frame count equals 5 s times the chosen fps

k-loop-seam.text: The frame at 5 s matches the first frame in position, color and scale for every animated property.

test.spec: pixel difference between first and last rendered frame is zero in animated regions

k-flash-limit.text: No more than three flashes occur in any one-second period.

test.spec: count luminance or red-flash transitions in every 1 s window; maximum is 3

k-reduced-motion.text: A reduced-motion path holds still or fades rather than looping the movement.

test.spec: CSS contains a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce block that sets animation to none or a static state

k-no-3d-gloss.text: Shapes read as flat vector with hairline or soft-shadow depth, not a 3D glossy render.

test.spec: no specular highlights or gloss on any shape

k-soft-gradients.text: Gradients are soft fields, not neon blobs.

test.spec: gradients blend across soft ranges with no saturated glow edge

k-settle-not-bounce.text: Motion travels a designed path and settles; it does not read as a bouncing spinner.

test.spec: the motion has one designed path and an ease-out settle, with no repeated vertical bounce

k-no-random-burst.text: A few shapes travel one designed path; there is no random confetti burst.

test.spec: shape count stays small and each shape follows a set path

k-no-logo.text: No Figma logo or wordmark appears as a mark.

test.spec: no Figma logo or wordmark is visible in any frame

k-shapes-primitive.text: Compositions use a small set of primitive solid shapes.

test.spec: every shape is a basic solid (circle, square, blob, starburst) with no decorative detail

k-palette-spectrum.text: Color draws from a wide spectrum, with the signature purple used by emphasis rather than as a fixed pairing.

test.spec: at least four hues appear across the loop and purple marks one emphasized element

k-shape-action.text: Motion animates an action or flow: a shape moves, reorders or activates as a stand-in for a real operation.

test.spec: each movement can be named as a meaningful action, not decoration

oq-brand-hex.text: Brand hex values: the fetched Figma page gives none. Search snippets list values from third-party sites, unfetched, so none are used. Check Figma's brand page before filling palette values.

oq-brand-hex-official.text: The fetched brand page gives no hex values; the palette entries are sampled from moodboard images, not official values. Check Figma's brand guidelines before publishing exact colors.

p-loop-5s.text: The deliverable is an animation of 5 seconds that loops.

p-figma-style.term: in the style of Figma brand visuals
p-figma-style.anchor: in the style of Figma brand visuals
p-figma-style.text: The look is the style of Figma brand visuals.

motion_principles._about: Discipline rung: motion design. Principles a senior motion designer applies, written from knowledge; the sourced parts are the accessibility entries.

pr-disney-timing.text: Disney-style animation principles: anticipation, slow in and slow out, follow-through, and arcs make motion read as physical.
behaviors: A shape that settles into place eases out, so the last 20 percent of the move is slow
A 5 s loop gives each beat its own ease instead of one curve for everything
pr-disney-timing.principle: Motion reads as weight and intent only when acceleration changes over time.
signals: linear easing on a brand mark
every element on the same curve

pr-motion-never-rests.text: How much a loop holds still is a reading, not a rule: a held beat gives the eye a resting point, while continuous motion keeps every frame moving.

readings.reading: holds between moves: the eye gets a resting point
readings.in_practice: Hold the logo still for about 0.5 s inside the 5 s loop, one moving element at a time, still beats between moves
signals: one moving element at a time

readings.reading: continuous motion: a flowing drift with no stop
readings.in_practice: Shapes keep drifting or orbiting through the loop with no hold, for an energetic, never-settling feel

pr-motion-never-rests.principle: Rest is what lets a viewer register the state the motion is leading to, and a continuous loop is a valid choice when the brand reads as energetic.

loop_motion._about: How a 5 second loop is built: frame budget, seam, easing, beats, and the readings of 'looping'. Builder options sit in the options area.

options._about: options, not requirements: builder choices where the prompt and evidence are silent

opt-cyclic-orbit.reading: cyclic loop where the end state equals the start
opt-cyclic-orbit.text: One shape orbits a centre point once in 5 s, eased evenly so the seam is invisible.

opt-pingpong-scale.reading: ping-pong loop that plays forward then back
opt-pingpong-scale.text: A shape grows for 2.5 s and shrinks back over 2.5 s.

opt-travel-wrap.reading: shape travel that exits one edge and returns from the other
opt-travel-wrap.text: A colored disc crosses the frame from left to right in 5 s and re-enters from the left as it exits.

opt-stepped-holds.text: Four poses held for 1.25 s each, changing on the beat.

opt-beats-a.term: beat plan A: out and back
opt-beats-a.text: Hold 0.5 s, move out over 2 s ease-out, hold 0.5 s, move back over 2 s ease-in-out. Sums to 5 s.

opt-beats-b.text: Hold 0.5 s, move out 1.5 s ease-out, hold 1.0 s, move back 1.5 s ease-in-out, hold 0.5 s. Sums to 5 s.

lm-loop-types.text: A cyclic loop suits motion that returns to its start, a ping-pong loop suits motion that retraces its path, and shape travel suits a shape that leaves one edge and re-enters the other.
properties: cyclic loop: end state equals start
seam hidden in ping-pong and travel
behaviors: A ping-pong loop doubles the play length: two 2.5 s legs give one 5 s pass
A shape-travel seam is hidden off-screen, so it needs the shape's exit and entry to match in speed
lm-loop-types.principle: The loop type decides where the seam can hide: in the state itself, in the reversal, or outside the frame.
signals: one shape moving in a closed path
a shape exiting frame and returning from the other side

lm-looping-quality.text: The word looping can mean four different motion structures, and each needs its own seam.

readings.reading: cyclic loop where the end state equals the start
readings.in_practice: every property returns to its frame-0 value at 5 s

readings.reading: ping-pong loop that plays forward then back
readings.in_practice: the reversal hides the seam and the play length doubles

readings.reading: shape travel that exits one edge and returns from the other

readings.in_practice: discrete poses on a fixed count, held between jumps
signals: poses on a grid of frames

pr-loop-seam.text: The loop seam is the join between the last and first frame; it should match exactly or the repeat jumps.
behaviors: A cyclic loop returns every property to its frame-0 value at 5 s
A ping-pong loop plays forward then backward, so its seam is hidden but its duration doubles
Most looping failures are a visible jump at the restart, usually from an object whose end position differs from its start
pr-loop-seam.principle: A loop is a closed curve in state space; a mismatch at the join reads as a jump on every repeat.
signals: visible jump when the clip restarts
start and end frames differ in position, color or opacity

lm-frame-budget.term: frame budget of a 5 second loop
lm-frame-budget.text: A 5 s loop is 120 frames at 24 fps, 150 at 30 fps and 300 at 60 fps; each beat is a frame span of that total.
behaviors: Animating on twos at 24 fps leaves 60 distinct drawings in the 5 s loop
A 0.5 s hold is 12 frames at 24 fps and 15 at 30 fps
lm-frame-budget.principle: Writing beats as frame spans makes the seam check exact: the last frame index is fps times 5 minus one.
signals: loop length given in seconds only
beat boundaries not on a frame

lm-seam.term: seam technique for a 5 s loop
lm-seam.text: Make frame 0 and the frame at 5 s identical for every animated property, then check the two frames side by side before shipping.
properties: position, scale, opacity and color match
end frame excluded from the repeat
behaviors: Render the last frame once and the first frame once and compare them with a difference view
Keep the duplicate frame out of the export so the repeat does not hold for two frames
lm-seam.principle: The restart is where a loop most often fails, so the seam is verified before anything else.
signals: opacity or color differs at frame 0 and frame 120
lm-seam.invariant: every animated property equals its frame-0 value at 5 s
lm-seam.variable: the path, the easing and the beat timing between frame 0 and 5 s

lm-easing-return.term: easing for a loop that returns to its start
lm-easing-return.text: A loop that moves out and back should ease out on the way out and ease in and out on the return, and each segment should end at zero velocity so the restart is continuous.
behaviors: A linear segment that ends at the seam makes the restart visibly jolt
A symmetric out-and-back uses the same curve reversed for the return
lm-easing-return.principle: Velocity should match at the join as well as position, or the eye reads the repeat as a stop and a start.
signals: motion still moving at the seam

accessibility_of_motion._about: Discipline rung: accessibility of motion. Sourced entries cite fetched pages.

pr-three-flashes.text: WCAG 2.3.1 (Level A) limits flashing content to no more than three flashes in any one-second period, unless flashes stay below the general and red flash thresholds.
behaviors: A brand sparkle or strobe that flashes fast and bright in a 5 s loop can break the limit even if it lasts under a second
Count opposing luminance changes, not just on-off cycles
pr-three-flashes.principle: Flashing can trigger seizures in people with photosensitive epilepsy, so it cannot be allowed even briefly.
signals: more than three bright flashes in one second

heading_path: Understanding SC 2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold (Level A)

pr-reduced-motion.text: The prefers-reduced-motion media query lets a page detect the OS setting that asks for less non-essential motion, and swap or remove the animation.
behaviors: Under reduce, the 5 s loop becomes a still frame or a short fade rather than travel and scale
Scaling and panning large objects are the named vestibular triggers
pr-reduced-motion.principle: Motion that moves large areas can cause discomfort for people with vestibular disorders; the setting is the user's stated preference.
signals: no reduce branch in the CSS
large scale or pan on load

brand_visual_identity._about: Discipline rung: brand visual identity, color and shape systems.

pr-color-shape-system.term: color and shape systems in brand identity
pr-color-shape-system.text: A brand system fixes a small palette of named colors and a limited vocabulary of shapes, and reuses them across every motion piece.
behaviors: The loop reuses the palette roles rather than new hues, so it reads as the same brand in every frame
pr-color-shape-system.principle: Recognition comes from repetition of a few fixed elements, not from novelty in each piece.
signals: more than four hues in one loop

brand_look._about: The look of the reference brand visuals, distilled brand-agnostically. Collected facts are tier 1-2; readings and exemplars sit in the options area.

options._about: options, not requirements: exemplars for each quality reading, to pick and mix; a consumer may sample at most two

bl-opt-gradient-exemplar.reading: bright multi-color geometric shapes on soft gradients
bl-opt-gradient-exemplar.text: Three overlapping flat circles and one rounded square over a soft blue-to-peach gradient.

bl-opt-hairline-exemplar.reading: flat shapes with hairline or soft-shadow depth
bl-opt-hairline-exemplar.text: One large flat orange blob with a 1 px dark outline and a single soft shadow beneath it, on warm grey.

bl-opt-playful-exemplar.text: A chunky lime starburst that scales in past a maroon circle, then the circle slides out, with a staggered handwritten aside.

bl-opt-precise-exemplar.text: Four equal squares snap to a grid, one slides to a new cell with a slow ease-out, the rest hold still.

bs-vocab.text: Bold, playful, varied flat-shape visuals meant to read as a language, not a fixed system.
bs-vocab.principle: A language lets one element be recombined in many ways; a rigid system predicts every use.

bs-primitives.text: A small set of basic solid shapes, from ambiguous blobs to representational forms, combined into compositions.
behaviors: A shape moves between passive, activated and hyper-activated states
Activation adds pattern, then wider color
bs-primitives.principle: Shapes are the protagonists; state changes give them behavior without new art.
signals: one pattern-filled shape among plain ones

bs-color.text: A wide, principled color spectrum with a signature purple kept, used by emphasis rather than one fixed pairing.
behaviors: Maximalist color is saved for emphasis
Color schemes adapt through variables
bs-color.principle: A spectrum with rules serves more contexts than one owned color pair.
signals: several saturated hues in one frame
a neutral ground behind bright shapes

tokens.hex: not stated on the fetched page

bs-composition.text: Shapes arranged as activities in one shared space, with corner handles and selection-style cues.
behaviors: Square nodes become circles when an object is being edited
Selected objects can expose and interact with other objects
bs-composition.principle: Selection and editing cues from the product, turned into shape, make the brand feel native to the tool.
signals: a circle where a square was

bs-motion.text: Motion animates actions and flows: a shape moves, reorders or activates as a stand-in for a real operation.
behaviors: Motion mirrors a tool action (select, move, reorder) rather than decoration
Motion is one of four named brand foundations
bs-motion.principle: Motion that performs an action teaches the action; motion for its own sake is noise.
signals: a shape that moves then settles
a shape that changes layer order

bs-type.text: Four type families: a grotesque, a condensed, a monospace and a handwritten face.
bs-type.principle: Each family covers one register: headline, dense label, code or data, human note.

lexicon._about: Vocabulary and associations for a 5 s looping motion piece in the style of Figma brand visuals. Seed material: options and words to draw on, not requirements.

lx-core-technical.text: A 5 s motion piece whose last frame hands back to its first with no visible jump.
lx-core-technical.principle: Matching start and end state is what makes a repeat feel continuous.

lx-perceptual-emotional.text: Words people use for the feel of brand motion, from playful bounce to calm settle.
signals: several saturated hues in one frame

lx-brand-shapes.text: Brand visuals built from a few primitive shapes, color spectrum and gradient fields, combined and recombined.
behaviors: A shape changes state by adding pattern, then wider color
Gradients drift slowly behind solid shapes to add depth without a shadow

lx-search.text: Phrases people type when looking for this kind of loop or brand motion.

lx-influences.text: Lineages that share the brand's geometric, flat and kinetic approach. Borrow what each brings rather than copying a style.

contribution.Saul Bass title design: reduced flat shapes built around one idea
contribution.Memphis Group: playful color clashes and patterned shapes
contribution.Swiss International style: a tidy grid and disciplined spacing
contribution.After Effects motion practice: easing curves as a shared vocabulary

lx-associations.text: Images that come to mind for the feel of the loop. Seed material to sample, not a fact.

exclusion._about: What a typical output gets wrong for a 5 s looping brand animation. Forbidden shortcuts with a check; the scoped anti-keywords sit in anti_keywords.

ex-cut-seam-is-loop.text: A looped clip with a cut at the seam is not a seamless loop.
behaviors: The eye finds the cut on the second repeat even when the first looks fine
ex-cut-seam-is-loop.principle: A loop is judged at the seam, not in the middle of the clip.
signals: frame difference at the seam above the rest of the clip
ex-cut-seam-is-loop.check: Compare the last frame with the first frame: positions, colors and shape counts match, or the seam is a cut.

ex-gif-stills-is-animation.text: A slideshow of still frames exported as a GIF is not motion on screen.
ex-gif-stills-is-animation.principle: Motion needs in-between frames that the eye reads as movement.
signals: hard jumps between frames with no intermediate positions
ex-gif-stills-is-animation.check: Count distinct positions per second across the loop: a shape moves through intermediate positions between keyframes.
